transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

What finally made me come in is my appetite has been really up and down for months. There are stretches where I skip dinner and lose weight without trying, and then other nights I just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels pointless.
Over these past months, have you also been feeling down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I guess I've lost interest in a lot of things. I still water my garden or go to book club sometimes, but it feels flat. Usually I leave early, or I just don't get myself to start in the first place.
How many weeks or months have you been experiencing this low mood and loss of interest?
Since my divorce was finalized—about a year and seven months now.
Since your divorce, have there been any weeks or months where your mood and interest returned to normal, or has it felt low and flat pretty much continuously the whole time?
It’s felt low and flat pretty much the whole time since the divorce was finalized—about a year and seven months.
Besides the appetite changes, have you noticed any other physical symptoms like feeling unusually hot, sweating more than usual, a racing heart, or trembling hands?
No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Before your divorce, had you ever gone through a similar period of low mood and loss of interest that lasted several weeks or more, followed by a return to feeling normal?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a similar time before then that lasted weeks like that.
Have you noticed changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual, since your mood has been low?
I can fall asleep okay, usually. But I keep waking up around four in the morning, thinking about bills, work notes, or the divorce, and then I’m just lying there exhausted until the alarm goes off.
Have you had any thoughts of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts about death or that you'd be better off not being here?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But sometimes I catch myself thinking it might be a relief not to wake up. That scares me, honestly—if one of my clients said that, I’d take it seriously.
Over these past months, have you noticed your energy is very low or that you have real trouble concentrating on tasks nearly every day?
Yes. Even when my caseload isn’t especially heavy, I feel like I’m dragging myself through the hospital. By the time I get home, I’m too tired to cook, stretch, or even answer personal messages.
Have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have you felt physically restless or unable to sit still, nearly every day during this time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself being unusually restless or anything, and no one’s said I seem different in that way.
